newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shanghai Ind firm on injection hopes.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai Ind firm on injection hopes.

text.p: Shares of Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd defied weak market sentiment to rise on Monday on buying fueled by hopes of future asset injections, brokers said.
"Hope of more asset injections in future, particularly following the recent asset purchase, fueled buying," said a sales director at a regional brokerage.
"Investors were seen interested in China plays in an absence of buying incentives for blue-chips," he said.
Shanghai Industrial shares were up HK$1.40 or 3.71 percent to HK$39.10 in late trade after they hit a new high of HK$39.30. Volume was 5.7 million shares worth HK$220.26 million.
The blue-chip Hang Seng Index was down 1.92 percent to 12,276.15 in late trade.

Last week, Shanghai Industrial said it would by a 35 percent stake in two roads in Shanghai for US$600 million, which would be financed by the issue of 139.47 million new shares at HK$34.18 per share.
Analysts generally said the deal would have a positive impact over the company's earnings in the long run.
